claims.assertion: The rider cancelled this RydeX trip, so the fee can only stand under NS-0/NS-4 (instant booking, rider cancellation), and it is chargeable only if the cancellation came more than 3 minutes after matching; the record shows acceptance at 08:40:00 and rider cancellation at 08:46:40, i.e. 6 min 40 s, which is outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window.

Because the booking was cancelled by the rider, the driver-supported no-show route to a $6.61 fee (NS-1) is not the operative basis, and nothing in the timeline shows a rider no-show at the pickup point; the rider's own message at 08:45 states plans changed and that the rider would cancel, and the recorded basis for the charge is the rider's own cancellation.

Ryde has published no rule that a driver's not-yet-arrival entitles a rider to free cancellation, so the rider's ETA-based fairness argument cannot by itself defeat the $6.61; the rider's remedy is the NS-7 human/voucher process, and the fee, if upheld, is issued as a $6.61 voucher rather than cash.

The rider's account history does not aggravate the case: no-show disputes in 90 days are 0 upheld, so this is not a repeated-fee pattern on the rider's side and no account flag against the rider is warranted.

The driver's tap-side conduct is not challenged by the rider as a NS-1 breach: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup (within the 200 m data-layer radius) and remained within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and the rider does not allege the driver failed to arrive or gamed the waiting/cancellation button.

weaknesses: The system records cut against the rider: F4 shows cancellation 6 min 40 s after acceptance, beyond the 3-minute free window in NS-4, and F7 confirms the $6.61 was actually charged, so the fee stands under the policy as written unless Ryde exercises its NS-7 discretion.

F1, F2, F3 and F6 show the driver genuinely was at/near the pickup (39–41 m, 200 m radius, single continuous stationary period 08:42:00–08:46:40) with no GPS gap, so the rider cannot argue the driver never arrived or that NS-1's arrival/waiting conditions failed; the rider's 'driver had not even arrived' framing in the complaint is contradicted by these system records.

The rider's own message F10 ('plans changed, I will cancel') is an admission of a rider-side change of mind, not a driver fault, and NS-8 (driver-late free cancellation) is informational only and cannot be cited, so the fairness argument has no clause support.

There is no route-deviation issue to bargain with: with cancellation by the rider before any trip, the route tools show no off-route segments and no extra distance, so no offsetting refund under RD-2 is available.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled a trip that had already been matched for 6 min 40 s; under NS-0 the case runs on the rider-cancellation branch because cancelled_by = rider, and the only question is whether the 3-minute free window was still open.

The cancellation came at 08:46:40, more than 3 minutes after acceptance at 08:40:00, so the free-cancellation window in NS-4 had closed and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands as recorded on the fare record (F7).
The driver was at the pickup point, not absent: he tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point, and GPS put his closest approach at 39 m at 08:46:10.
The driver waited far beyond the 3-minute benchmark: he was stationary 08:42:00–08:46:40 at 41 m from the pickup (4 min 40 s) and was within 200 m cumulatively for 5 min 15 s before the cancellation.

The rider's own message at 08:45 — "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" — is her admission that the cancellation was for personal convenience, not because the driver failed to arrive, and no delay, traffic or weather excuse appears in the records (F15 fair weather, no incidents).

That the rider raised this dispute does not create a waiver: NS-8's driver-late exemption is an information-only clause from other operators that Ryde does not adopt, and the driver had in fact been on site for minutes, so nothing in NS-4/NS-7 assists her.
The driver reported his position in chat at 08:42 ("At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis"), so the rider cannot claim she was never told the car was waiting when she cancelled three minutes later.

weaknesses: The strongest point for the other side is F6 taken together with F2/F5: the driver tapped "I'm Here" only at 08:42:15, and although GPS already showed him 40 m from the pickup at that moment, a rider could argue the strict NS-1 (iii) window ('waited >3 min after the tap') ran only 4 min 25 s to the cancellation — this case is not a driver-cancellation no-show, so NS-1's fee is not what is being charged, but the judge will read F6 either way.

The cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver (F4), so the NS-1/NS-2 analysis the driver would prefer (which validates the $6.61 as a no-show fee of which $4.50 goes to the driver) does not strictly apply; the fee here is sustained only under the NS-4 3-minute rule, which is a thinner basis than a confirmed no-show.

The rider's message F10 comes only after the driver's F9 and is a courtesy notice rather than a dispute of arrival; if the judge reads "plans changed" as evidence the rider was never meaningfully given a chance to board, the decision could soften toward the NS-7 human review rather than a clean no_action.

The driver's written statement F12 ("parked at the pickup for minutes") is a bare statement that would lose to the record; I rely only on F2/F3/F6, and if the GPS coverage of the wait were found incomplete the wait claim would fall.

Driver profile F17 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days; although profile facts cannot decide the case, the judge may treat the pattern as a reason to scrutinise the timing evidence rather than accept it.

events.body: The fee in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee, and the record settles the branch: cancelled_by = rider at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s (400 s) after acceptance at 08:40:00 [F4][F7]. Under NS-0 the rider-cancellation branch is the only route into the NS clauses, and it is an instant booking, so the applicable test is NS-4 [F4][F7][NS-0][NS-4]. NS-4 charges nothing only if the rider cancels within 3 minutes of matching; 400 s exceeds 180 s, so the $6.61 stands as recorded on the fare record [F4][F7][NS-4]. The rider's fairness argument — that the driver "had not even arrived" — is contradicted by the system records, which override statements: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and was stationary 41 m from the pickup from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 [F2][F3][F6][NS-4]. Her own message at 08:45 — "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" — is a rider-side change of mind, not a driver fault, and the driver had already reported his position in chat at 08:42 [F9][F10][NS-4]. I read the two-message chat (both timestamped) and the driver's post-trip statement; the driver's statement that he "was parked at the pickup for minutes" is consistent with, and in any event subordinate to, the GPS/timeline records [F11][F12][F2][F3]. No NS-1 no-show fee is being justified here: the charge rests on the rider's own cancellation, though the same records show the driver's on-site presence if that branch were tested [F4][F6][NS-1][NS-0]. Because the cancellation is chargeable at 400 s and no refund flows from any clause, the amount is $0.00 (no computation: the fee is validated, not reduced) [F4][F7][NS-4]. The rider's profile (0 upheld no-show disputes) is not used against her and is not decisive either way [F16][NS-4]. No safety issue arises on the screen: I read chat #1 and chat #2, the driver's written statement and the complaint, and found no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-cancellation fee under NS-4; no refund or waiver; advise the rider via RydeHELP that any discretionary goodwill review is a matter for Ryde under NS-7.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled this RydeX trip, so the fee can only stand under NS-0/NS-4 (instant booking, rider cancellation), and it is chargeable only if the cancellation came more than 3 minutes after matching; the record shows acceptance at 08:40:00 and rider cancellation at 08:46:40, i.e. 6 min 40 s, which is outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window.

Because the booking was cancelled by the rider, the driver-supported no-show route to a $6.61 fee (NS-1) is not the operative basis, and nothing in the timeline shows a rider no-show at the pickup point; the rider's own message at 08:45 states plans changed and that the rider would cancel, and the recorded basis for the charge is the rider's own cancellation.

Ryde has published no rule that a driver's not-yet-arrival entitles a rider to free cancellation, so the rider's ETA-based fairness argument cannot by itself defeat the $6.61; the rider's remedy is the NS-7 human/voucher process, and the fee, if upheld, is issued as a $6.61 voucher rather than cash.

The rider's account history does not aggravate the case: no-show disputes in 90 days are 0 upheld, so this is not a repeated-fee pattern on the rider's side and no account flag against the rider is warranted.

The driver's tap-side conduct is not challenged by the rider as a NS-1 breach: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup (within the 200 m data-layer radius) and remained within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and the rider does not allege the driver failed to arrive or gamed the waiting/cancellation button.

weaknesses: The system records cut against the rider: F4 shows cancellation 6 min 40 s after acceptance, beyond the 3-minute free window in NS-4, and F7 confirms the $6.61 was actually charged, so the fee stands under the policy as written unless Ryde exercises its NS-7 discretion.

F1, F2, F3 and F6 show the driver genuinely was at/near the pickup (39–41 m, 200 m radius, single continuous stationary period 08:42:00–08:46:40) with no GPS gap, so the rider cannot argue the driver never arrived or that NS-1's arrival/waiting conditions failed; the rider's 'driver had not even arrived' framing in the complaint is contradicted by these system records.

The rider's own message F10 ('plans changed, I will cancel') is an admission of a rider-side change of mind, not a driver fault, and NS-8 (driver-late free cancellation) is informational only and cannot be cited, so the fairness argument has no clause support.

There is no route-deviation issue to bargain with: with cancellation by the rider before any trip, the route tools show no off-route segments and no extra distance, so no offsetting refund under RD-2 is available.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled a trip that had already been matched for 6 min 40 s; under NS-0 the case runs on the rider-cancellation branch because cancelled_by = rider, and the only question is whether the 3-minute free window was still open.

The cancellation came at 08:46:40, more than 3 minutes after acceptance at 08:40:00, so the free-cancellation window in NS-4 had closed and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands as recorded on the fare record (F7).
The driver was at the pickup point, not absent: he tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point, and GPS put his closest approach at 39 m at 08:46:10.
The driver waited far beyond the 3-minute benchmark: he was stationary 08:42:00–08:46:40 at 41 m from the pickup (4 min 40 s) and was within 200 m cumulatively for 5 min 15 s before the cancellation.

The rider's own message at 08:45 — "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" — is her admission that the cancellation was for personal convenience, not because the driver failed to arrive, and no delay, traffic or weather excuse appears in the records (F15 fair weather, no incidents).

That the rider raised this dispute does not create a waiver: NS-8's driver-late exemption is an information-only clause from other operators that Ryde does not adopt, and the driver had in fact been on site for minutes, so nothing in NS-4/NS-7 assists her.
The driver reported his position in chat at 08:42 ("At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis"), so the rider cannot claim she was never told the car was waiting when she cancelled three minutes later.

weaknesses: The strongest point for the other side is F6 taken together with F2/F5: the driver tapped "I'm Here" only at 08:42:15, and although GPS already showed him 40 m from the pickup at that moment, a rider could argue the strict NS-1 (iii) window ('waited >3 min after the tap') ran only 4 min 25 s to the cancellation — this case is not a driver-cancellation no-show, so NS-1's fee is not what is being charged, but the judge will read F6 either way.

The cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver (F4), so the NS-1/NS-2 analysis the driver would prefer (which validates the $6.61 as a no-show fee of which $4.50 goes to the driver) does not strictly apply; the fee here is sustained only under the NS-4 3-minute rule, which is a thinner basis than a confirmed no-show.

The rider's message F10 comes only after the driver's F9 and is a courtesy notice rather than a dispute of arrival; if the judge reads "plans changed" as evidence the rider was never meaningfully given a chance to board, the decision could soften toward the NS-7 human review rather than a clean no_action.

The driver's written statement F12 ("parked at the pickup for minutes") is a bare statement that would lose to the record; I rely only on F2/F3/F6, and if the GPS coverage of the wait were found incomplete the wait claim would fall.

Driver profile F17 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days; although profile facts cannot decide the case, the judge may treat the pattern as a reason to scrutinise the timing evidence rather than accept it.

points.response: Conceded as a matter of the applicable branch: F4 shows cancelled_by = rider, so the case runs on the rider-cancellation branch (NS-0) and no-show clauses are not the basis for the charge.

Accepted on the fee's arithmetic: F4 puts acceptance at 08:40:00 and the rider's cancellation at 08:46:40, i.e. 6 min 40 s, past the 3-minute free window in NS-4, so the $6.61 in F7 cannot be struck down on the 3-minute ground.

The rider does not contest the driver's presence: F6 (tap at 08:42:15, 40 m from pickup) and F1 (closest approach 39 m at 08:46:10) confirm the car was on site, but D3 uses these facts to argue an NS-1 no-show that is not the branch the fee was charged under (F4, rider-cancelled), so it adds nothing to the NS-4 analysis.

D4 recites the NS-1 no-show conditions (F3 stationary 08:42:00-08:46:40; F2 within 200 m for 5 min 15 s), but by the driver's own admission and F4 this was a rider-initiated cancellation, so NS-1's $6.61 no-show fee - of which $4.50 would go to the driver - is not what is being justified and could not be retro-fitted here.

F10 does read as a rider-side change of plans, and the rider does not deny it; but F10 also shows the rider told the driver at 08:45 and cancelled by her own hand at 08:46:40 (F4), so no driver fault exists - which is precisely why the rider asks for Ryde's discretionary review under NS-7 rather than asserting a breach.

Accepted that NS-8 is information-only and cannot be cited; the rider's case is therefore that she has no legal ground against the $6.61 and instead asks the judge to route the fairness point to human review under NS-7, which the driver's F2/F6 presence facts do not close off.

F9 shows the driver's 08:42 message about his position and the rider does not dispute receiving it, so no failure-to-notify claim is made; D7 is therefore not in issue and does not strengthen the case beyond what F4 already establishes.

Withdrawing nothing, but refining C3: since F4 shows the fee rests solely on the rider-cancellation branch (NS-4) rather than on any driver fault, the rider's sole remaining request is that the $6.61 be treated as a discretionary waiver/voucher question for Ryde under NS-7 rather than a policy breach by the driver.

Accepted as correct and supportive of my client: the rider's cancellation at 08:46:40 (F4) falls outside the 3-minute free window measured from acceptance at 08:40:00, so the $6.61 fee on the fare record (F7) stands under NS-4.

I agree the operative basis is the rider's own cancellation branch, not NS-1; the driver's on-site conduct nevertheless removes any suggestion of fault on his side, since the fee is chargeable under NS-4 on the rider's cancellation alone (F4, F10).

No dispute: Ryde publishes no driver-late exemption, the rider's fairness argument has no clause support, and NS-7 makes any refund a $6.61 voucher at Ryde's discretion rather than cash — which is exactly why the charged fee (F7) should be left undisturbed.
Agreed; the rider's profile (F16: 0 upheld no-show disputes) is not used against her and my client seeks no flag against the rider, only confirmation of the fee.

Correct on the records: the tap at 08:42:15 was made 40 m from the pickup (F6), closest approach 39 m (F1), and the driver was within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap and stationary at 41 m from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 (F3) — the rider's complaint that he 'had not even arrived' is contradicted by GPS, and the rider raises no NS-1 breach because none exists.
